exposure: Caseload midwifery group vs. standard midwifery care group
Women with similar distance to the hospital
cohort: All-risk singleton births in two maternity units in the North Denmark Region between 2013 and 2016
finding: While there were no differences in most labour outcomes between caseload midwifery and standard care, slightly higher rates of augmentation and adverse neonatal outcomes were observed in the caseload midwifery group.
mod_finding: Compared to standard midwifery care, caseload midwifery was associated with more frequent augmentation of labor and emergency cesarean sections, but no differences were observed for elective cesarean sections, preterm birth, induction of labor, dilatation of cervix on admission, amniotomy, epidural analgesia, and instrumental deliveries.
